zh-CN.Two Similar Calculations With Different: Two Similar Calculations With Different Meanings
zh-CN.A drawer or inset component may fail to: A drawer or inset component may fail to fit even when every recorded dimension looks precise. The first task is to distinguish a specification from a measurement statement. NIST Technical Note 1297, Section 5 [1], describes combined standard uncertainty, while its propagation appendix [2] includes sensitivity coefficients and covariance. This article applies those concepts to an original cabinet dimension chain. The example is hypothetical and does not prescribe hardware clearances. It shows why adding maximum dimensional limits and combining standard uncertainties answer different questions, even when both calculations happen to use millimeters.
zh-CN.Write the Dimension Chain Before the Bud: Write the Dimension Chain Before the Budget
zh-CN.Let W be an outside cabinet width, tL an: Let W be an outside cabinet width, tL and tR the side thicknesses, and P an inset component width. Define the combined remaining side clearance C = W − tL − tR − P. For assumed values W = 600.0 mm, tL = tR = 18.0 mm, and P = 562.0 mm, the nominal total clearance is 2.0 mm. This is the combined clearance, not an automatic 1.0 mm allocation to each side: alignment and installation determine that division. Hardware instructions and functional requirements must establish the acceptable range before this chain becomes a release check.
Suppose the permitted deviations are ±0.5 mm for W, ±0.2 mm for each thickness, and ±0.4 mm for P. All adverse extremes can reduce clearance by 0.5 + 0.2 + 0.2 + 0.4 = 1.3 mm. The chain therefore permits a minimum of 0.7 mm and a maximum of 3.3 mm under these assumed dimensional limits. This calculation makes no probability claim. It asks what the permitted extremes allow. Whether that interval is acceptable depends on the real assembly requirement, including centering, straightness, finish buildup, and other effects not yet represented in the four-term model.
zh-CN.Now consider a measurement result with s: Now consider a measurement result with standard uncertainties u(W) = 0.30 mm, u(tL) = u(tR) = 0.15 mm, and u(P) = 0.20 mm. These are new assumed measurement inputs, not the previous tolerance limits relabeled. If the inputs are uncorrelated and the linear model is adequate, u(C) = √[0.30² + 0.15² + 0.15² + 0.20²] = 0.418 mm. This describes a combined standard uncertainty associated with the result. It is not a guaranteed bound, a manufacturing tolerance, or a complete conformity decision. An expanded uncertainty would also need its coverage factor and justified interpretation.
zh-CN.A Shared Thickness Error Changes the Ans: A Shared Thickness Error Changes the Answer
zh-CN.Suppose the thickness uncertainties inst: Suppose the thickness uncertainties instead arise entirely from one common source, so the left and right thickness inputs have correlation +1, while W and P remain uncorrelated with them. Their combined thickness contribution is then 2 × 0.15 = 0.30 mm, giving u(C) = √[0.30² + 0.30² + 0.20²] = 0.469 mm. Real budgets often contain both shared and independent components; they require an explicit covariance treatment. Simply reading both pieces with the same caliper does not establish this exact correlation. The constructed case illustrates why independence needs evidence rather than being a convenient default.
zh-CN.NIST's method combines uncertainty compo: NIST's method combines uncertainty components through a measurement model and accounts for correlations where relevant. It also distinguishes combined standard uncertainty from expanded uncertainty. The original cabinet examples above use those principles but do not inherit a NIST endorsement or calibration status. A tolerance interval needs its own specification basis. If only maximum error limits are available, converting them into standard uncertainties requires an appropriate distributional model and other assumptions. Do not insert the limits directly into a statistical formula and then interpret the result as a guaranteed fit.
zh-CN.Make a Measurement Plan That Can Be Audi: Make a Measurement Plan That Can Be Audited
zh-CN.Identify the reference surfaces for W, t: Identify the reference surfaces for W, tL, tR, and P and state when each is measured. A width before edging or finishing is not necessarily the installed width. Record instrument identification, checks, reading technique, environmental conditions where relevant, and repeated positions across the assembly. Separate observed variation from uncertainty in a measurement of one dimension. Preserve raw readings and shared correction terms so another reviewer can rebuild the chain. If the dimension chain omits a relevant feature such as a bowed side, add that physical issue explicitly rather than trying to hide it inside an arbitrary uncertainty allowance.
zh-CN.Use Each Result for Its Own Decision: Use Each Result for Its Own Decision
zh-CN.A worst-case review can reveal that perm: A worst-case review can reveal that permitted part dimensions do not ensure the required functional clearance. A measurement uncertainty budget can reveal that available measurements cannot distinguish a marginal fit with enough confidence. The remedies differ: revise dimensional limits or geometry for the first problem, and improve the measurement or decision procedure for the second. A complete release also addresses the applicable hardware and an explicit acceptance rule. Neither the 0.418 mm figure nor the 0.7 mm lower clearance by itself approves a drawer. Their value is making the unresolved part of the decision precise.
